youtube.title: The US Army Fought Hitler With Balloons | The Ghost Army
youtube.description:
In 1944, about 1,100 American soldiers of the 23rd Headquarters Special Troops, many recruited from art schools and ad agencies, went to war with inflatable tanks, fake artillery, recorded sound effects and fake radio traffic. On their final mission at the Rhine, they impersonated about 40,000 men with more than 600 inflatable vehicles. Their work stayed classified for decades. They are credited with saving thousands of lives, and received the Congressional Gold Medal in 2024.

📂 Case File #016: The Ghost Army

Sources: Ghost Army Congressional Gold Medal Act (H.R. 2170, govinfo.gov); Stars and Stripes (Jan 2022); Hyperallergic.
Images: Ghost Army Congressional Gold Medal design (public domain); Rhine crossing 1945 (public domain); WWII decoy landing craft (public domain); Ellsworth Kelly by Jeremiah Garcia, CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons).
Narration voice: AI.
